description: Estudiantes de preparatoria con altas capacidades visibles, nos impulsa la creatividad, innovación y las ganas de explorar nuevos horizontes.
summary:
We have developed a virtual library featuring an interactive 3D space in which users can move around freely. It was built using C++ and some Python. The 3D models and various other modeling assets were sourced from free repositories or directly from NASA. Information and APA-style citations are presented on a lectern-style display. We chose C++ because it offers greater flexibility for creating 3D environments and animations, while also providing superior resource management and version control across platforms such as Windows, Linux, Android, and iOS. The project will be available on GitHub upon completion.
The project addresses the challenge by telling accessible stories, enabling children to learn about and develop an interest in space, NASA’s activities, and past missions. We use language that is easily understood by young children and have structured the content as short stories tailored to different age groups.
This initiative is important for sparking an interest in space-related topics among new generations, ensuring the experience is neither tedious nor overly complex; in this way, we cultivate curiosity while allowing for a gradual, natural development of their understanding.
details:
Starry Library is an interactive 3D desktop library designed to make reading and learning about space more immersive. Instead of presenting information as a traditional website or digital document, users can explore a virtual library, walk between rooms, select books from shelves or searchable catalogs, and open them in an interactive reading view.

The library contains two connected areas: a children’s room with 40 interactive books and a teen/adult room with 19 longer readings. The stories cover topics such as Mars, Europa, the Moon, Saturn, spacecraft, solar activity, Earth observation, and NASA missions.

One of the main creative elements of the project is the use of animated 3D pop-up scenes inside the books. Rockets, rovers, satellites, antennas, and other objects unfold from the pages and animate while the user reads. The goal is to combine the feeling of a physical pop-up book with the possibilities of a real-time 3D application.

Starry Library was developed primarily in C++20 using SDL2, OpenGL 3.3, and Cairo. The project includes custom rendering, camera movement, collision detection, book interaction, page turning, 3D OBJ models, shaders, catalogs, and animation systems. GitHub and GitHub Actions are also used for version control and automated Linux and Windows builds and tests.

The application supports both English and Spanish and allows users to switch languages while using the program. During development, we considered performance, ease of navigation, visual consistency, readability, cross-platform compatibility, and how to make educational content engaging without making the interface unnecessarily complicated.

Our intended impact is to encourage students to explore astronomy, space science, and reading through an experience that feels more like discovering a real library than simply reading information from a screen.
